narrative: The model estimated an 83% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, and because law school admission here is tied to that prediction, your application was denied. The strongest factor was your part-time status: nearly 93% of accepted students were full-time, and being part-time pushed the prediction toward failure. The next most important factor was your Year 3 class standing. Your third-year decile of 3 is well below the accepted-student average of about 5.8, and that lower relative academic performance also pushed toward failure. Family income was the third-ranked factor and had a smaller but still unfavorable effect: coming from a middle-income background was associated with a modest push toward failure, though accepted students were more often upper-middle income (45.4%) than middle income (34.8%). Other profile details had less influence on this decision. To improve your chances, ask admissions for specific feedback and consider whether you can study full-time or significantly reduce work hours during bar preparation. You should also speak with an academic adviser about strengthening your upper-year academic record and whether additional coursework, an LSAT retake, or a later application cycle would make your profile more competitive. Provide context for part-time work or financial constraints if relevant, and focus your reapplication plan on the factors that most strongly affected this outcome.
